articles.title: Moment family rescued after 16 hours floating on jet ski off Thailand
articles.excerpt: A 50-year-old father and his two sons have been rescued after they were found adrift off the Thai island of Koh Samui, a local official told AFP on Saturday. They had spent more than 16 hours floating at sea after their jet ski capsized, local government official Amorn Chomchoey said. "We found the exhausted after swallowing a lot of seawater," he told the news agency, adding "they were pale, especially the boys". The family were checked in hospital after being rescued and were discharged shortly afterwards, Chomchoey told AFP.

articles.title: Zimbabwe boat accident death toll hits 68 as 22 more bodies recovered
articles.excerpt: Twenty-two more bodies have been recovered after a boat accident in Zimbabwe, taking the death toll to 68, police said on Saturday.The ferry capsized on Tuesday on Lake Kariba, on the border with Zambia. An investigation has suggested it was overloaded when it turned over during heavy winds.Eighteen children were among the people killed, Zimbabwe’s police said, in what is believed to be the country’s deadliest such disaster.Most of the passengers are believed to be villagers and fish traders who lived around the lake.Officials said the vessel was authorised to carry 90 people but was packed with 114 adults, five crew members and an unspecified number of children.Lt Col Joseph Muchechesi, commander of the boat regiment involved in the search operation, said: “So far today we have managed to take 22 bodies. We are confident that we will manage to retrieve all the bodies.”The civil protection unit said on Wednesday that 77 people had been rescued.Hundreds of people gathered at the district hospital in the lakeside town of Kariba to identify the bodies of their relatives and loved ones.Family members walk past caskets carrying their loved ones during a memorial service for the victims of the boat accident in Kariba, Zimbabwe, 13 August 2026. Photograph: Mkhululi Thobela/APA public memorial service was held in Kariba, nearly 280km (175 miles) north-west of the capital Harare, on Thursday before the burials started.Survivors said they pleaded with the ferry driver to turn back as the vessel had begun taking on water soon after departing.Chance Siyamavhu, 45, told Agence France-Presse: “Thank God that a wave pushed the sinking vessel and we managed to climb on top.“When the boat capsized, most of the people scrambled to get the lifejackets but most of them did not even know how to use them.“Most people could not make it.”Lake Kariba is the world’s largest manmade lake by volume.

articles.title: Moroccan police arrest more than 100 people as they attempt to enter Ceuta
articles.excerpt: Moroccan police have arrested 111 people as they tried to enter Spain’s north African territory of Ceuta, amid ⁠tightened security on both sides after social media posts ​called for another mass crossing.The attempted crossing on Saturday came two weeks after more than 72,000 migrants surged into Ceuta, causing tensions within the EU and prompting anti-immigration rhetoric among far-right parties worldwide. At least 96 people died trying to ⁠reach European soil.A source in Morocco’s interior ministry told news agency Reuters that those detained included 109 migrants from sub-Saharan Africa and two Moroccan citizens arrested in or around Fnideq, the Moroccan city near Ceuta.Moroccan police used teargas to disperse groups of migrants ⁠gathered on hills about 1.9 miles (3km) from the border, according to Spanish news agency EFE. Reuters later saw hundreds of police officers, some in riot gear and others in plainclothes, returning from the hills outside ​Fnideq.EFE and Spanish state broadcaster TVE said Morocco’s interior ministry ordered their journalists ‌to leave Fnideq immediately, without providing an explanation.Witnesses said they saw teargas being fired at migrants on hills near the border. Photograph: Jalal Morchidi/EPAIn Ceuta, ‌Spanish soldiers guarded supermarkets while police patrolled the main streets. The city was calmer than in the days after the deadly crossing attempt on 30 July.Madrid has ‌since installed a maritime barrier and deployed more than 500 additional police officers from mainland Spain, raising the total in Ceuta to more than 1,600. The interior ministry said the reinforcements would remain for as long as needed.“We’ll continue to deploy whatever personnel are necessary to restore normality as soon as possible and prevent events like those of 30 July from happening again,” Spain’s interior minister, Fernando Grande-Marlaska, said on Thursday.About 5,000 migrants remained in Ceuta, the minister added.

articles.title: American missionary kidnapped in Niger freed after nine months
articles.excerpt: An American missionary who was kidnapped in Niger in October has been released, his organisation has said.Serving in Mission International said Kevin Rideout “is in good health in the care of US officials” and would soon be reunited with his extended family.Donald Trump, who claimed to have helped secure Rideout’s release, later said he was “back in United States Custody” on Friday.The 50-year-old missionary pilot was kidnapped in the west African country’s capital, Niamey, on 21 October by three armed individuals and was probably driven out of town, according to a security official at the time. No armed group claimed responsibility for the abduction. Other details about his rescue remain unknown.The US president’s administration had made the release of Rideout a priority in its latest strategy on African Sahel states, after years of fighting extremism found limited success. Rideout had been working in Niger for 19 years as a missionary before the incident.The American missionary Kevin Rideout is said to now be in safe hands. Photograph: Hostage Aid Worldwide“I am proud to announce that Kevin Rideout, a wonderful Christian Missionary, is back in United States Custody,” Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform on Friday. “Kevin, the United States of America looks forward to welcoming you HOME. Glad to have helped!”Niger has long been the target of attacks by armed groups, including jihadis linked to al-Qaida and Islamic State. A “continually deteriorating security situation” across the country was cited by the military junta that took power in 2023 when deposing the democratically elected president, Mohamed Bazoum.The new authorities ousted western partners, including the US, which had soldiers in Niger, and forged a new security and diplomatic alliance with Russia.

articles.title: DRC’s fast-growing Ebola outbreak spreads to sixth province
articles.excerpt: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has spread to a sixth province, officials have said, a day after the head of the World Health Organization said the outbreak was on track to surpass the deadliest in history, which killed at least 11,000 people more than a decade ago.The current outbreak has killed more than 2,100 people out of more than 4,500 cases, according to the latest government figures released on Tuesday. At the same point in the 2014-16 outbreak in west Africa, the previous most deadly outbreak, 755 cases had been recorded, according to WHO data.Jean Kaseya, the director general of Africa CDC, said on Thursday that a death had been recorded in the previously unaffected Bas-Uele province. The man had travelled from Isiro, in Haut-Uele province, to Buta, the capital of Bas-Uele, where he died, Kaseya said.There are no approved vaccines or treatments for the rare Bundibugyo strain of the virus that is responsible for the current outbreak.The death toll has been reached almost three times faster than in the 2014-16 outbreak. On Wednesday, Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, the WHO director general, said the current outbreak would surpass that one based on its current pace.Six of DRC’s 26 provinces have now been affected, mainly those along the country’s north-eastern border. More than 3,400 of the cases have been recorded in Ituri province, where the outbreak was first reported.Uganda has reported 20 cases, all in the capital, Kampala.

articles.title: French ambassador to CAR investigated over claims he hosted dozens of women
articles.excerpt: France has opened disciplinary proceedings against its ambassador to Central African Republic over allegations of misconduct, after claims he brought dozens of women into his official residence, raising potential security concerns.The investigation comes as Paris seeks to rebuild relations with CAR after their sharp deterioration in recent years amid Russia’s expanding influence in the former French colony.The French weekly newspaper Le Canard enchaîné reported that the ambassador, Bruno Foucher, 65, brought about 30 women between the ages of 20 and 30 into his residence during the period of January 2024 to March 2026, with some of them staying overnight. The visits prompted officials to report a security breach.The ambassador acknowledged having had sexual relations with two young women, the weekly said.The French foreign ministry said: “At the initiative of the ministry, an administrative investigation was carried out in Bangui in 2026. Upon receipt of the findings of this mission, and at the request of the minister, the ministry initiated disciplinary proceedings against the ambassador. These proceedings are ongoing.”The ministry conducted an on-site inspection in April, which led to the opening of disciplinary proceedings.Foucher is a career diplomat who has served as ambassador to CAR since 2023.

articles.title: Brazil’s Lula launches historic fourth term bid – but son of jailed Bolsonaro stands in his way
articles.excerpt: Brazil’s leftwing president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, has launched his campaign for a historic fourth term and vowed that as long as he lived he would not allow the “shameless” right to return to power.Addressing a sea of supporters in São Bernardo do Campo, the industrial city where his political career began nearly half a century ago, the 80-year-old politician reminded voters of the chaos and violence that unfolded during the 2018-22 presidency of his far-right predecessor, Jair Bolsonaro, whose son Flávio Bolsonaro will face Lula in October’s presidential election.Lula recalled how hundreds of thousands of citizens died during a Covid outbreak Jair Bolsonaro was accused of bungling with his anti-science policies. Gun ownership soared as laws were relaxed, allowing criminal groups to expand their arsenals. “They handed out … more than a million weapons,” Lula said, promising to dedicate a fourth term to improving education and healthcare as well as developing Brazil’s rare-earth deposits, the world’s second largest after China’s.Lula launched his re-election campaign at the Vila Euclides football stadium, where his rise to the presidency began in 1979 as a union leader. Photograph: Sebastião Moreira/EPALula also said he would improve security by targeting the rich organised crime bosses who lived in luxury apartments. “It’s easy to kill a crook in a favela. But the guy running the show lives in a penthouse … and we need to stop this,” Lula said. He also told his far-right rivals to “show some shame”.Lula was speaking at the Vila Euclides football stadium, where his astonishing rise to the presidency began in 1979 when, as 33-year-old union leader, he spearheaded two historic strikes that helped end the military dictatorship.

articles.title: Ontario free to axe Toronto bike lanes, region’s top court rules
articles.excerpt: The Ontario government is now free to rip out Toronto’s bike lanes on its busiest streets after the region’s top court ruled in favour of the province on Friday, overturning a lower court’s decision that decreed removal would violate constitutional rights.The win is significant for Ontario’s premier, Doug Ford, and his government, who have long railed against Toronto’s bike lanes, blaming the protected zones for the city’s traffic ills.In 2024, the Ford government passed legislation that would allow Ontario to axe Toronto’s lanes, despite the recent installation of the infrastructure by the municipality.But the effort to tear up the lanes covering 19km (12 miles) of road was paused after cycling advocacy organisations levelled a legal challenge against the province.Their challenge was supported in July 2025, when a superior court judge ruled removing the lanes was unconstitutional, as it would create a heightened risk of death or injury, in turn violating the right to life and security of the person. Those rights are protected under Canada’s Charter of Rights and Freedoms.Friday’s decision from the Ontario court of appeal reverses that ruling. Michael Longfield, executive director of Cycle Toronto, one of the groups that launched the legal challenge, said he is disappointed in the decision.“This isn’t just about keeping people on bikes safe. It helps pedestrians. It helps other drivers. It has a very strong traffic calming effect that we need in major cities,” he said.The court of appeal judges in their decision wrote that there is no charter right to bike lanes and the government is free to change legislation on the lanes if it wishes.

articles.title: Canadian plasma clinics pause collections after deaths of two donors
articles.excerpt: A chain of private plasma donation clinics in Canada has said it is pausing collections after the deaths of two donors and a new government investigation into potential unsafe practices.Grifols, a Spanish healthcare company which runs 17 clinics in Canada and is the country’s only private clinic for plasma donation, said it informed Health Canada of its decision to temporarily pause collections on Wednesday.On the same day, the agency had issued a formal notice of non-compliance for failure to follow blood regulations, a senior official told the Globe and Mail newspaper.The two deaths occurred after plasma donations in October 2025 and January 2026, Health Canada said in March of this year. The donors, both of whom were in the province of Manitoba, went into “distress” while donating, people familiar with the cases said.Though Health Canada did not release the identities of the donors, friends said one was Rodiyat Alabede, 22, an international student and aspiring social worker who donated plasma in Winnipeg on 25 October.Patient advocates reported at the end of May that there were concerns about whether Alabede had been properly screened.“They had staff taking plasma from donors who did not know how to extract plasma in a safe manner,” alleged Kat Lanteigne, a safe blood campaigner who represents Alabede’s family.“The [failures] were so egregious that … now we have more questions than answers,” she said in May.An autopsy showed Alabede died of cardiac arrest shortly after donating.

articles.title: BP to develop offshore gasfield in Venezuela with firms linked to Trump administration
articles.excerpt: BP has answered Donald Trump’s call for oil companies to help rebuild Venezuela’s fossil fuel industry with new plans to develop a large offshore gasfield.BP will partner with two oil firms with close links to the Trump administration to develop the second phase of the Loran gasfield, in one of the first large-scale foreign investments in Venezuela since the US ousted its leader Nicolás Maduro in January.The London-listed oil company holds a licence to develop the field alongside a Qatari company owned by the Al-Khayyat brothers, the Syrian-born billionaires working with Ivanka Trump, the US president’s daughter, and her husband, Jared Kushner, to build a controversial multibillion-dollar resort in Albania.BP will also work alongside the overseas investment arm of UAE’s national oil company run by the industry minister, Sultan Al Jaber, who in 2025 promised Trump that the Gulf state would increase its investments in the US energy sector more than sixfold to $440bn (£325bn) within a decade.The deal makes BP one of the first large-scale international oil firms to return to Venezuela after rival Shell secured a licence to develop the first phase of the Loran field earlier this summer. Caracas is also in talks over oil projects with the Italian oil company Eni.Meg O’Neill, BP’s chief executive, described the licence as “an important step forward” in the company’s collaboration with Caracas, which “reflects the progress we have made together”.BP is one of a handful of European oil firms that have returned to the basin since Trump called for foreign oil companies to invest “at least $100bn” to help rebuild and tap Venezuela’s oil resources after capturing the country’s former president.The US oil companies ExxonMobil and ConocoPhillips have begun scouting opportunities in Venezuela, but have been slower to play a role in its fossil fuel revival after the Latin American country nationalised the industry in 2007.

articles.title: Former Mexican governor charged in case of 43 students who vanished in 2014
articles.excerpt: The former governor of Guerrero state in Mexico has been formally charged over his alleged involvement in the disappearance of 43 students in 2014, a case that has become a symbol of the country’s brutal cartel violence and government impunity.Ángel Aguirre, who was arrested last week, is accused of forced disappearance and obstruction of justice for ordering the destruction of surveillance tapes that may have shed light on what happened to the students from the Ayotzinapa teacher training college on the night of 26 September 2014.On Wednesday, a judge ruled Mexico’s attorney general had presented enough evidence to formally charge Aguirre with forced disappearance and ordered that he remain in a maximum security prison awaiting trial.A lawyer for Aguirre denied his client’s wrongdoing. Guillermo Baradas told reporters: “We presented evidence demonstrating a high-level meeting attended by Mr Ángel Aguirre at the time the videos were allegedly handed over to him.”Aguirre’s indictment is the biggest breakthrough in the Ayotzinapa case since the 2022 arrest of Jesús Murillo Karam, who served as Mexico’s attorney general at the time of the students’ abduction.The brutality of the case rocked Mexico and continues to haunt the country more than a decade on. With the remains of only three students identified, it is not known what happened to the 40 others.On the night that they were abducted, the students from the Raúl Isidros Burgos teacher training college in the village of Ayotzinapa had commandeered several buses in the city of Iguala to get to a protest in Mexico City.But before they could leave Iguala, in Guerrero state, the students were attacked by a local criminal gang working with municipal police.

articles.title: Japan’s defence minister heads to Australia to meet Marles in wake of melon-gate controversy
articles.excerpt: Japan’s defence minister will visit Canberra this week, the highest level engagement with Australia after controversy over Anthony Albanese’s comments about a gift of melons from prime minister Sanae Takaichi.The defence minister, Shinjiro Koizumi, will meet his counterpart and deputy prime minister, Richard Marles, on Tuesday, with discussions focused on Australia’s acquisition of Japan’s Mogami-class frigates and enhanced security cooperation.Koizumi is considered a potential future prime minister of Japan.

articles.title: Rescue teams search for survivors in Indonesia after powerful earthquake
articles.excerpt: Rescue crews dug through collapsed buildings and landslide debris in eastern Indonesia on Sunday as they searched for bodies and possible survivors a day after a powerful earthquake killed at least 53 people, injured more than 100 and displaced thousands.At least 24 people died in Manggarai regency and 17 in neighbouring East Manggarai, with additional fatalities reported in Sikka, Ngada and Ende regencies, the national disaster management agency said. Rescuers were still searching for people feared buried beneath landslides triggered by the quake across six regencies on Flores, a predominantly Catholic island in Muslim-majority Indonesia.The magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck 68km (42 miles) north-northwest of Ende in East Nusa Tenggara province, the USGS said. The quake, at a depth of about 10km (6 miles) off the coast of Flores, rattled much of the island and sent residents fleeing in panic. Tremors were also felt in neighbouring West Nusa Tenggara and parts of southern Sulawesi.A crack in the road in East Nusa Tenggara after the quake. Photograph: Ignasius Kunda/EPAThe disaster agency said the quake destroyed more than 900 homes and damaged nearly 450 more, forcing about 5,000 people into temporary shelters. Thousands more spent the night outdoors, fearing strong aftershocks. At least 167 public facilities, including schools, health centres and churches, were also damaged.Relief workers have begun distributing rice, ready-to-eat meals, drinking water, blankets and medicine, while emergency shelters were being set up for displaced residents. Authorities said restoring electricity and communications as well as delivering aid to remote villages isolated by landslides remained among the biggest challenges.Earthquake victims are treated in a temporary medical tent amid fears of aftershocks in Ruteng. Photograph: Juni Kriswanto/AFP/Getty ImagesThe quake also struck Labuan Bajo, the gateway to Komodo national park, one of Indonesia’s best-known tourist destinations.

articles.title: Powerful earthquake kills dozens in eastern Indonesia
articles.excerpt: A 7.7-magnitude earthquake that struck eastern Indonesia has killed at least 47 people, causing widespread panic and collapsing buildings and homes in a region prone to deadly seismic events.Rescuers have yet to reach Nagekeo, the area closest to the epicentre, because roads were blocked by landslides and communications disrupted.Authorities issued a tsunami warning, which has since been lifted, but there were at least 235 aftershocks, including one of magnitude 6.1. Indonesian authorities said monitoring showed no significant sea level changes that could indicate a tsunami.A motorcyclist rides past a crack in a road in East Nusa Tenggara province. Photograph: Ignasius Kunda/EPATsunami waves of ⁠ 1.5 metres (3ft) were recorded in several areas.The Indonesian geophysics agency, BMKG, recorded the first quake at 4.58am on Saturday local time at a depth of 9 miles (15km) in the country’s Flores region.A second earthquake of magnitude 6.1 struck off northern Sumatra, Indonesia, hours after the initial quake, with no casualties yet reported.Rescuers around the port town of Maumere found 20 people dead, six severely injured and two trapped under the rubble, said Fathur Rahman, the head of the city’s rescue agency. Eight of those dead had been killed in a landslide. Maumere is the main town in Sikka regency on Flores Island in the east of Indonesia’s vast archipelago.Patients are treated in the hallway of a hospital in Labuan Bajo, East Nusa Tenggara province. Photograph: Firdia Lisnawati/APA video on Facebook, verified by Reuters as being at a port in Maumere, shows parts of a building collapsing as people scream and run in the street.

articles.title: ‘Unprecedented’ rain kills five in Japan as thousands stranded at airport
articles.excerpt: At least five people have died in eastern Japan after “unprecedented” heavy rain that left nearly 7,000 stranded at Tokyo’s Narita airport and forced thousands to take refuge in government buildings.The torrential rains hit Chiba prefecture, east of Tokyo, on Thursday night, triggering landslide warnings and power outages. Evacuation orders were issued for more than 400,000 people in Chiba and other areas, and about 45,000 homes lost power, as 115mm of rain fell hourly, approximately the same amount usually recorded for the whole month of August.It was the first time the Japan Meteorological Agency has issued the highest level-5 warning for heavy rains and landslides for the prefecture.The body of a man, believed to be in his 60s or 70s, was found floating in a flooded road in the city of Ichikawa, while a 66-year-old woman was killed when her car got trapped in flood waters in the city of Sakura. Two other people are reported to have died after being unable to escape from their cars during the flooding. Soldiers have been dispatched to the area ‌to help with relief efforts.“This case was an extremely unusual situation,” Chiba governor Toshihito Kumagai told reporters on Friday morning. “I have responded to many disasters in the past, but I have never experienced a case like this.”A makeshift evacuation centre set up at the Chiba prefectural government building after transport was disrupted by the torrential rain. Photograph: Kyodo/ReutersApproximately 7,000 passengers spent the night at Narita, one of Tokyo’s main international airports, while 1,700 people sought shelter at the Chiba prefectural government building.Footage from public broadcaster NHK showed water spurting violently from what appeared to be a maintenance hole and exceeding the height of a nearby five-storey building in Chiba’s central ward.Flooded areas after heavy rain in Chiba prefecture.

articles.title: Indonesia wildfires threaten orangutans rescued from animal traffickers
articles.excerpt: Orangutans rescued from wildlife traffickers face a new threat from the record number of fires that have broken out in Indonesia in recent weeks.Flames have come within metres of an animal rehabilitation centre in West Kalimantan as hot, dry and windy conditions have been amplified by a powerful El Niño and the human-driven climate crisis.In the first 13 days of August, Indonesia registered more than three times more forest fire hotspots than in the whole of the same month last year. This followed a record number of blazes between January and July.West Kalimantan has been at the epicentre. After 40 days without rain, there have been dozens of severe outbreaks of fire in the region.Orangutans at the Yiari rehabilitation centre. Photograph: YiariFlames threatened the Yiari orangutan rehabilitation centre this week. The fire moved rapidly from 1km away to within 100 metres of the perimeter within days, prompting staff to relocate the 60 resident orangutans to enclosures in the middle of the centre.Indonesia authorities have water-bombed the forest to try to control the blaze, and teams from the centre joined the firefighting efforts as the air quality worsened, posing a threat to animals and the wider ecosystem.The centre’s director, Dr Karmele Llano Sánchez, said in her latest update that battling the fire had been relentless. “We were fighting it until 3am, but this morning it has reignited. The teams are working round the clock but they are exhausted.”The situation had reportedly stabilised as of Thursday evening, with all the animals safe, but the meteorological agency has said the hot, dry conditions are likely to continue and could lead to more outbreaks.Indonesian authorities have urged people to avoid setting fires and to remain vigilant because the peak of the fire season is usually in September and October.Yiari is seeking funds for more firefighting equipment.

articles.title: Australia politics live: NSW to fast-track datacentre approvals; ANU announces Julie Bishop replacement
articles.excerpt: From 1h agoNSW framework commits to 75 day assessments for datacentres who meet ‘world-class’ standardsPenry BuckleyThe NSW has committed to assessing new datacentre proposals within 75 days if they meet “world-class” energy, water and environmental standards, under a framework announced today.The Minns government’s new datacentre guidelines follow the prime minister’s announcement last month of a national office of AI and regulatory framework for datacentres, amid growing community concern about land, water and power use by the rapidly expanding industry.The Minns government has credited investment in datacentres, which has increased 75% per year on average over the last three years, as the reason NSW has avoided recession.A datacenter construction site in Artarmon, Sydney. Photograph: Mick Tsikas/AAPUnder the NSW guidelines, the planning department will commit to assessing proposals within 75 days if datacentre builders comply with six principles, including applying “world-class environmental and efficiency standards”, imposing no net cost to consumers and communities and funding additional water and energy supply.Under the guidelines, they must “demonstrate a commitment to training and skills to support jobs”. The government says developments will still need to meet planning, environmental and community consultation standards.The state government says it will introduce regulation to make sure datacentres pay for electricity network upgrades without the cost being passed on to households and small businesses. It has not made the same commitment on the cost of providing water, but will commission the independent pricing regulator, Ipart, to review “how water pricing can reflect the full costs associated with servicing datacentres”, including management of the impacts of drought.The framework has already been endorsed by datacentre companies CDC, AirTrunk, and Data Centres Australia.
articles.summary: 新南威尔士州承诺，根据今日宣布的框架，若数据中心提案符合「世界级」能源、水和环境标准，将在75天内完成评估。明斯政府的这一新数据中心指导方针，是在总理上个月宣布设立国家AI办公室及数据中心监管框架之后出台的，此前社区对快速扩张的数据中心行业占用土地、水资源和电力的问题日益担忧。明斯政府将数据中心投资（过去三年平均每年增长75%）视为新州避免衰退的原因。根据该指导方针，规划部门将承诺在75天内评估提案，前提是数据中心建设方遵守六项原则，包括采用「世界级环境与效率标准」、不对消费者和社区造成净成本，以及为额外的水和能源供应提供资金。他们还必须「展示对培训和技能以支持就业的承诺」。政府表示，开发项目仍需满足规划、环境和社区咨询标准。州政府表示将引入监管，确保数据中心支付电网升级费用，而不会将成本转嫁给家庭和小型企业。但在供水成本方面未作同样承诺，不过将委托独立定价监管机构Ipart审查「水价如何反映服务数据中心的相关全部成本」，包括干旱影响的管控。该框架已获得数据中心公司CDC、AirTrunk和Data Centres Australia的认可。

articles.title: Nazi artefacts still being sold online years after trade outlawed across Australia
articles.excerpt: Nazi artefacts bearing prohibited symbols are being openly sold in Australia three years after the federal government made it illegal to do so, with vendors saying they are doing so for “educational” reasons.The government in 2023 outlawed the display and trade of items bearing the Nazi Hakenkreuz (swastika) and double-sig rune that was the logo of the Schutzstaffel (SS), after multiple states passed similar laws that banned the display of Nazi symbols and the performance of the Nazi salute.The laws included exemptions for religious, academic, educational, artistic, literary or scientific purposes.Guardian Australia has identified Australian sellers of military antiques listing German military items – including helmets, badges, medals, officer’s caps, flags and more – that appear to be from the Nazi era and which bear the Hakenkreuz or double-sig rune.The vendors, which include longtime dealers of military collectibles and Nazi objects, claimed to be selling the items for “educational” or “research purposes”.Kurt Coleman Military Antiques, a business with a registered address in Queensland’s Sunshine Coast region, had 25 pages of Nazi-era German military and related items for sale on its website as of this week.The listings included military booklets, pins, badges, rings, officer’s tunics, officer’s caps and weaponry with visible swastikas and other Nazi imagery.One of the highest-priced items was a white porcelain vase with an embossed Nazi eagle for $2,500.

articles.title: Australian health experts fear US vaccine scepticism is catching on as ‘anything Trump says filters through’
articles.excerpt: Australian medical experts have warned a shift in child vaccination advice in the US is not grounded in science and could undo decades of public health advances.The US president, Donald Trump, signed an unprecedented executive order calling for American children to be vaccinated against fewer diseases, suggesting a link to autism despite no evidence. The official number of recommended immunisations for children would drop to 11, compared with 18 at the end of 2024.Six of those shots would be recommended for all children in the US, while the five others would only be recommended for high-risk children, including hepatitis B.Australia currently recommends 15 childhood vaccinations, all of which health experts say are key to protecting children’s health.Prof Julie Leask, a social scientist at the University of Sydney and an expert on social behaviours surrounding vaccination, said Trump’s decision, and his broader embrace of the US health secretary and vaccine opponent, Robert F Kennedy Jr, are threats to vaccine uptake in Australia.“Anything Trump says filters through to Australia,” Leask said. “Australian parents and caregivers hear it, and it does affect a minority of people and makes them wonder about vaccines and their safety.”Leask, a trained midwife, has studied vaccination rates for decades. She said health professionals are already seeing the impacts of Trump’s rhetoric in Australia, with nurses saying they hear from more and more parents who have concerns about vaccination.“Some of my colleagues are worried that we’re kind of going back to the future,” she said.A national survey of Australian parents released in February showed parents were less accepting of routine childhood vaccinations than they were in the previous year.Figures from the Australian immunisation register show full childhood vaccination rates peaking between 2020 and 2021.

articles.title: The PM called Sally McManus a giant of the Labor movement. Now she just wants to go birding
articles.excerpt: Sally McManus started her job as the country’s most powerful trade union leader amid howls of criticism.Shouted down for suggesting union members were right to break “unjust” industrial laws in a live TV interview, McManus quickly adjusted to the high-decibel work of being secretary of the Australian Council of Trade Unions.Now, nearly a decade later, she is ready to turn the volume down.“I’m looking forward to having a break,” McManus told Guardian Australia before handing over the job at the end of the month.“It’s been 33 years as a union official, 22 of them as a leader, and nine-and-a-half as ACTU secretary. It never stops.”Sign up for the Breaking News Australia emailMcManus announced her departure last month, on the same day the ACTU president, Michele O’Neil, revealed plans to step down as well. Anthony Albanese described both – the first all-female leadership team in the ACTU’s 99-year history – as “giants of the labour movement”.McManus has helped reshape Australia’s industrial landscape, pushing the Albanese government and business on a worker-friendly agenda.Along with O’Neil, she has helped lead campaigns for same job, same pay protections, laws giving workers the right to disconnect, wage theft criminalisation and ensuring minimum pay, insurance and safety standards for gig economy workers.Her tenure has spanned the Turnbull, Morrison and Albanese governments, economic disruption from the Covid-19 pandemic, Labor’s jobs and skills summit, allegations of corruption and lawlessness by union leaders, including the CFMEU, and, a year ago this week, the productivity roundtable convened by the treasurer, Jim Chalmers.The ACTU president, Michele O’Neil, and the secretary, Sally McManus, during an economic reform roundtable last year.

articles.title: Logies 2026: Sam Pang wins gold and Sam Neill wins posthumous best actor at Australia’s TV awards
articles.excerpt: Sam Neill has won a posthumous best actor award at Australia’s biggest television awards, the Logies, with comedian Sam Pang taking home the night’s top honour, the Gold Logie award for most popular personality.Neill, who died in July, won his posthumous Logie for best lead actor in a drama, for his performance in legal thriller The Twelve: Cape Rock Killer. His close friend, the actor Heather Mitchell, accepted the award on his behalf.“I’m so sorry I’m not Sam,” she said. “I know how much it would mean to him. This is an indication of his connection with his audience.”Mitchell said The Twelve, which Neill starred in for three seasons, “meant a great deal” to him.“He really relished the character of Brett Colby. He talked about it a lot, and he thought [Colby] was a very clever man, and also a sort of 007 kind of person. And that was Sam as well,” she said.Heather Mitchell pays tribute to Sam Neill onstage at the Logies. Photograph: James Gourley/Getty Images for TV WEEKPang, who is a panellist on quiz show Have You Been Paying Attention? and hosts The Front Bar and Sam Pang Tonight, joked: “I’ve got lots of people to thank tonight and I’ll probably forget some names. If I do forget you, I’m sorry, but maybe also have a think about how much you did.”The 52-year-old congratulated his fellow nominees for the top award: A Current Affair host Ally Langdon, comedian Julia Morris, ABC presenter Lisa Millar, Masterchef judge Poh Ling Yeow, presenter Robert Irwin and Tipping Point Australia host Todd Woodbridge.Pang was presented the award by Magda Szubanski, who made a surprise appearance after recently announcing she was in remission after being treated for cancer.Magda Szubanski in character as her Kath & Kim role Sharon Strzelecki with Robert Irwin onstage.

articles.title: Five teenagers killed after car driven on wrong side of Irish motorway
articles.excerpt: Five teenagers have died and four other people have been seriously injured in a crash involving a car driving in the wrong direction on a motorway in the Republic of Ireland, police said.Gardaí confirmed the bodies of the youths, all male, had been removed from the scene of the two-vehicle collision, which happened at about 3am on Sunday on the M9 in County Kildare.The force said the occupants of the second vehicle involved, three women, two in their 30s and one in her 20s, and a boy, all remained in hospital with serious injuries.The Garda commissioner, Justin Kelly, described the head-on collision between the two cars as “horrific” and said “in some cases” vehicles were being driven on the wrong side of motorways for social media likes.Last weekend, nine people were injured in a head-on collision on the M50 in Dublin involving a car travelling in the wrong direction.Describing Sunday’s crash, Kelly said: “These family members were travelling innocently when they were struck by a vehicle being driven the wrong way down the motorway.“This horrific incident, after the recent collision on the M50, shows how irresponsible and dangerous driving on the wrong side of the motorway is.“That, of course, should be self-evident, but what makes this reckless behaviour even more appalling is that in some cases it is being done for social media likes, regardless of the potentially devastating impact it might have on innocent people and themselves.”He added: “As this particular incident has been referred to Fiosrú, the police ombudsman, I am constrained in what I can say in detail about this incident, but I know that gardaí do what they can to stop such vehicles while also taking into consideration all other road users.“Gardaí are put in a really challenging situation dealing with such incidents.”Officers are investigating the circumstances of the crash, which happened at junction 3 of the motorway, near Athy, at about 3am on Sunday.Emergency services had been alerted to reports
articles.summary: 警方表示，爱尔兰共和国一条高速公路上发生一起逆向行驶车辆相撞事故，造成五名青少年死亡，另有四人重伤。警方确认，所有死者的遗体均为男性，已从事发现场移走。事故发生在周日凌晨约3点，地点为基尔代尔郡的M9高速公路。警方称，涉事第二辆车的乘员包括三名女性（两人30多岁，一人20多岁）和一名男孩，他们均因重伤住院。爱尔兰警察专员贾斯汀·凯利将这两车迎头相撞的事故描述为“可怕”，并表示“在某些情况下”，人们为了在社交媒体上获取点赞而在高速公路上逆向驾驶。上周末，都柏林M50高速公路上发生了一起逆向行驶车辆引发的迎头相撞事故，造成九人受伤。在描述周日的事故时，凯利表示：“这些家庭成员无辜行驶在路上，却遭到一辆在高速公路上逆向行驶的车辆撞击。”“这起可怕的事件，加上近期M50上的碰撞事故，表明在高速公路上逆向行驶是多么不负责任和危险。”“这当然是不言而喻的，但令这种鲁莽行为更加令人发指的是，在某些情况下，人们这样做只是为了在社交媒体上获得点赞，全然不顾这可能对无辜者和他们自己造成的毁灭性影响。”他补充说：“由于这起特定事件已提交给警察申诉专员Fiosrú，我对这起事件的详细评论受到限制，但我知道警察会尽最大努力阻止此类车辆，同时也会考虑所有其他道路使用者。”“警察在处理此类事件时处境非常艰难。”警方正在调查这起事故的具体情况，事故发生在周日凌晨约3点，地点为阿西附近高速公路3号交叉口。紧急服务部门已接到相关报告。

articles.title: Ukrainian drone attack on Russia kills at least six, says Moscow
articles.excerpt: Ukraine has launched one of its largest drone attacks since the start of the war, causing a fire at a distribution warehouse near Moscow and killing at least six people overnight, according to Russian authorities.The defence ministry in Moscow said it had shot down 1,478 Ukrainian drones in the past 24 hours – the highest ever total claimed – in an escalating air war in which seven Ukrainians were also killed as Russia bombed 13 locations inside the country.A huge fire engulfed a 250,000 sq metre building near Podolsk, 25 miles south of Moscow’s city centre, belonging to the Wildberries distribution company. The facility was disabled as a result, Ukraine’s military said.Sergei Sobyanin, the mayor of Moscow, said 600 drones targeted the Moscow region overnight, of which 201 were destroyed.

articles.title: Europe’s tallest Virgin Mary statue unveiled in small Polish village
articles.excerpt: An enormous statue of the Virgin Mary that is believed to be Europe’s tallest was inaugurated on Saturday in a small Polish village, in the presence of the anti-communist leader Lech Wałęsa.Hundreds of people took part in the consecration of the monument, which towers 55.6 metres (182ft) over Konotopie in central Poland, a village of fewer than 150 people.While helicopters scattered miniature red roses over the crowd, priests in white robes celebrated mass and the Mazowsze folk ensemble sang and danced to traditional Polish music.The statue is taller – if less dramatically located – than the Christ the Redeemer statue in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, which measures 38 metres including its pedestal. The Polish monument’s height includes a crown-shaped 15-metre pedestal.It also surpasses another large-scale religious monument in Poland, the Christ the King statue in the western town of Świebodzin, which was revealed in 2010 and, with the mound it stands on, is 52.5 metres tall.There is a taller statue of the Virgin Mary in the Philippines, which measures 98 metres. But the new one in Poland is believed to be the largest of its kind in Europe.The statue was paid for by a wealthy couple who live nearby. Photograph: Agnieszka Bielecka/EPAWałęsa, who won the Nobel peace prize for his leadership of the Polish anti-communist resistance as the head of the Solidarity trade union and was later Poland’s president, had a front-row seat during the inauguration ceremony.“This is the end of my path,” said Wałęsa, 82, suggesting the causes he had long championed, including democracy and the Catholic faith, were now completed. “I started with the Virgin Mary and I end with the Virgin Mary.”During his Solidarity days, Wałęsa famously wore a Black Madonna pin and he has often credited his faith in God with giving him the strength to fight against communism.Most Poles identify as Catholic.

articles.title: Renaissance paintings by Antonello da Messina stolen from Sicilian museum
articles.excerpt: Four of the most important works of art by the 15th-century Renaissance master Antonello da Messina were stolen during a national holiday from a museum in the Sicilian port city of Messina.Thieves gained access to the Regional Museum of Messina, or MuMe, on Saturday evening, possibly capitalising on attention being focused on La Vara, a huge religious festival that takes place in the city on 15 August, when Italy marks the Ferragosto national holiday.Bypassing the alarm systems, the gang broke into a security display box and stole four wood panels painted by Antonello, who is widely credited with changing the course of Renaissance art.Thieves took three of the five surviving panels that made up an altarpiece known as the Polittico di San Gregorio, one of the Sicilian painter’s most important works.The fourth, smaller stolen work, which depicts Virgin and Child. Photograph: Museo Regionale Accascina Messina/Reuters“It is an extremely serious and significant loss,” said Marisa Mercurio, the director of the museum. “They have stolen works of enormous cultural, artistic and symbolic importance, not only for Messina but for Sicily as a whole.

articles.title: Jared Kushner meets with Hamas ahead of talks with Netanyahu on Gaza
articles.excerpt: Donald Trump’s son-in-law and envoy, Jared Kushner, held a rare meeting with Hamas’s political chief on Sunday in Egypt, in a new diplomatic effort to make progress in the stalled Gaza ceasefire. Kushner will meet on Monday with Benjamin Netanyahu, who is under pressure after rejecting the new 15-point, US-backed road map.The talks aim to salvage the plan for Hamas to disarm and Israel to withdraw from the Palestinian territory shattered by war.At stake are the lives of some 2 million people in Gaza and reconstruction of the crowded enclave now largely controlled by Israeli forces, more than 10 months since the ceasefire ended major military operations. A meeting between Kushner, fellow envoy Steve Witkoff and Hamas leaders in Egypt last year helped clinch the ceasefire, whose progress until now had been stalled over the key issue of Hamas’s disarmament.The over two-hour meeting in Egypt with Hamas’s political chief, Khalil al-Hayya, was confirmed by a regional official and a Hamas official, both speaking on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to talk to reporters. Kushner was one of a trio of envoys meeting with al-Hayya, with officials from mediating countries Egypt, Qatar and Turkey also there.Hamas in a statement later called on mediators and the US-created Board of Peace overseeing the ceasefire to “compel” Israel to approve the road map for next steps.Netanyahu, the Israeli prime minister, last week rejected the 15-point plan in a rare public show of defiance against the Trump administration, Israel’s closest ally.Kushner; Tony Blair, the former British prime minister; and Nickolay Mladenov, the Board of Peace director, are to meet with Netanyahu on Monday, according to a source familiar with the plans and a diplomatic source.
articles.summary: 唐纳德·特朗普的女婿兼特使贾里德·库什纳周日在埃及与哈马斯政治领导人举行了罕见会晤，这是为推动陷入停滞的加沙停火取得进展而进行的新外交努力。库什纳将于周一与本雅明·内塔尼亚胡会面，后者在拒绝了美国支持的新的15点路线图后正面临压力。会谈旨在挽救哈马斯解除武装、以色列从这片饱受战争蹂躏的巴勒斯坦领土撤军的计划。事关加沙约200万人的生命，以及这片目前大部分由以色列军队控制的拥挤飞地的重建——停火结束主要军事行动至今已逾10个月。库什纳、同僚特使史蒂夫·维特科夫去年与哈马斯领导人在埃及的会晤促成了停火，但此后停火进程因哈马斯解除武装这一关键问题而陷入僵局。一名地区官员和一名哈马斯官员证实了与哈马斯政治领导人哈利勒·哈亚在埃及举行的两个多小时的会晤，两人均因未获授权向记者透露消息而要求匿名。库什纳是与哈亚会晤的三位特使之一，调停国埃及、卡塔尔和土耳其的官员也在场。哈马斯随后在一份声明中呼吁调停方和美国创建的监督停火的「和平委员会」「迫使」以色列批准下一步行动的路线图。以色列总理内塔尼亚胡上周拒绝了这项15点计划，这是罕见的公开违抗特朗普政府——以色列最亲密盟友——的表现。据知情人士和外交消息人士透露，库什纳、英国前首相托尼·布莱尔和和平委员会主任尼克莱·姆拉德诺夫将于周一与内塔尼亚胡会面。

articles.title: Israeli strikes on southern Lebanon kill 11 in worst toll since June truce
articles.excerpt: Eleven people have been killed, including three children, and 19 injured in two Israeli airstrikes on southern Lebanon, the worst toll since deals in June brought a lull in hostilities between Israel and Hezbollah.Israeli warplanes bombed a home on the outskirts of the village of Ansar, killing seven people and flattening the building early on Saturday morning. Rescue services were working at the site to try to find survivors and locate bodies.Another airstrike hours later on a home in the town of Deir al-Zahrani killed two, wounded nine and covered the streets in rubble and smoke. An Israeli drone also targeted a motorcycle in the nearby city of Nabatieh, but it was unclear if the driver was killed.The escalation came despite a June ceasefire in which most fighting between Israel and Hezbollah ended.Residents of southern Lebanon wondered if the attacks signalled further escalation to come or if it was safe to stay in their homes. Neither village was in Israel’s self-declared “security zone” – a 231-square-mile area occupied by its forces.The roads out of Nabatieh and the surrounding villages were choked with traffic after the strikes as people fled north in search of safety.The Israeli military spokesperson, Ella Waweya, said Israel had attacked “Hezbollah infrastructure” in the Ansar and Nabatieh area in response to the group’s fighters attacking soldiers in the Ali Taher area.Rescue workers and residents search for survivors after an Israeli airstrike on Deir al-Zahrani in southern Lebanon. Photograph: Abdul Kader Al Bay/Zuma Press Wire/ShutterstockAli Taher is a hill where the Israeli military says large underground Hezbollah command and control centres are located, and it has been shelling the area for months.The Lebanese prime minister, Nawaf Salam, condemned the Israeli attacks, calling them “extremely dangerous” and said they undermined efforts to establish stability in the south.He called on Israel to stop the escalation.

articles.title: Trump threatens to declare strait of Hormuz ‘territory of the United States’
articles.excerpt: Donald Trump has threatened to declare the strait of Hormuz as “a territory of the United States” as his administration struggles to conclude the war with Iran.During a speech at a police academy on Long Island, New York, on Friday, the US president said he would “pretty soon” designate the waterway – a crucial chokepoint for global trade, through which about a fifth of the world’s seaborne oil supplies typically pass – a US territory.The comment came as peace talks with Iran remain at an impasse following failed negotiations, with Tehran refusing to reopen the strait, which has been all but closed since the US and Israel launched their war on Iran in February.Almost six months into the war, there is little indication that negotiations will soon yield peace, as Iranian officials continue to defy Trump’s demands. The US has been blockading Iranian shipping and ⁠ports in recent months in an effort to pile economic pressure on Tehran.“After we finish defeating Iran, which is being very badly defeated, pretty soon I’ll be declaring the Hormuz strait a territory of the United States,” Trump said on Friday. “Essentially, that’s what it is. We have the blockade.

articles.title: Israeli military plans to transfer law enforcement in occupied West Bank to police
articles.excerpt: Israel’s defence minister wants to transfer law enforcement powers for Israelis in the occupied West Bank over to the police, a plan that Palestine’s vice-president described as a “flagrant violation of international law” and step towards full Israeli annexation.Israel Katz announced that he had ordered the military to draw up plans for the handover of responsibility for policing Israeli settlers amid domestic and international criticism of the army’s failure to tackle militants besieging three Palestinian families.The Palestinian vice-president, Hussein al-Sheikh, called for international intervention to enforce international law and stop a move that would “entrench the illegitimate annexation of Palestinian land”.Katz unveiled his plan as a settler siege in the Palestinian village of Qusra entered its sixth day. The Israeli army has proved unable or unwilling to remove the group of militants trying to drive out Palestinian residents through a campaign of terror.Israeli soldiers watch Israeli settlers setting up a tent just outside the entrance of a besieged Palestinian family home in the village of Qusra, in the Israeli-occupied West Bank, on 14 August 2026. Photograph: Jaafar Ashtiyeh/AFP/Getty ImagesMichael Sfard, a leading Israeli human rights lawyer, said a transfer of law enforcement powers could constitute a major step towards formal annexation.“The military can delegate enforcement but not responsibility [of the law],” Sfard said.

articles.title: Benjamin Netanyahu describes UK as ‘first Islamic republic to get a nuclear weapon’
articles.excerpt: The Israeli prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, called the UK “the Islamic republic of Britain” in a podcast interview, where he also described the country as the “first Islamic republic to get a nuclear weapon”.His comments, made during an interview for Israel’s army radio, played into a common far-right Islamophobic trope about Britain’s small Muslim population.Netanyahu praised positive coverage of Israel by the journalist Randolph Churchill, the son of former prime minister Winston Churchill, over half a century ago, then said: “Go find that in today’s Britain, in what is called the Islamic republic of Britain.”Rather than challenge Netanyahu’s comments, the host questioned whether he is unfairly singling out the UK, asking: “Isn’t all of Europe is like that?”Netanyahu replies by doubling down. “Yes, but you know someone said the first Islamic republic with nuclear weapons will be the Islamic republic of Britain.”Pakistan, officially the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, has had a nuclear arsenal since the 1990s.Relations between the UK and Israel have been increasingly strained in recent months, especially since Andy Burnham took over in No 10. Shortly before becoming prime minister, he apologised for Labour’s initial response to Israel’s military action in Gaza, saying the party “didn’t get it right” and needed to “do better” under his leadership, signalling a significant shift in the UK’s approach to the Middle East.In July, he said he would “do more to put pressure on the Israeli government”, including through further sanctions on individuals and entities, as well as a potential ban on the trade of goods with illegal settlements.The US vice-president JD Vance suggested the UK could become an ‘Islamist country’ in 2024.
